The market is beginning to recognize this momentum, as the stock is currently trading at the top of its 52-week range [E4]. The scanX signal engine confirms this bullish outlook by identifying that earnings growth is currently accelerating [E60]. The company is currently generating a negative return on equity of -41.58%, which stands in stark contrast to the sector benchmark of 9.95% [E8]. This lack of profitability is compounded by a return on assets of 0%, failing to meet the sector benchmark of 4.77% [E7]. Furthermore, the company’s long-term performance is marked by a compounded sales growth of -21% over the last decade, and the most recent trailing twelve months show a contraction of -29% [E13, E16]. Investors are also denied any income, as the dividend yield is 0.00% [E3]. Conceded: [E14, E15, E60]. The current valuation appears disconnected from these operational realities, as the stock is trading at the very top of its 52-week range [E4] while the scanX signal engine indicates that price growth is currently outpacing profit growth by 12% [E51].

Conceded: the company achieved a 50% compounded sales growth over 5 years and 44% over 3 years [E14, E15]. However, that short-term acceleration masks a severe 10-year compounded sales decline of -21% and a sharp TTM contraction of -29% [E13, E16]. The bull claims an attractive valuation via the 1.53x price-to-book ratio [E6], but ignores that this is paired with a disastrous return on equity of -41.58% and a zero percent return on assets against a 4.77% sector benchmark [E8, E7]. The stock sitting at 100% of its 52-week range [E4] alongside a negative P/E of -3.68x [E5] confirms the scanX warning that price growth exceeds profit growth by 12% and expectations are running ahead of delivery [E51]. Finally, the complete absence of any dividend yield [E3] leaves shareholders carrying all the operational risk without cash returns.
